full_judgment:
This appeal is directed against the order dated 31.8.77 passed by Additional District Judge, Rangpur in Misc. Appeal No. 25 of 1976, affirming the judgment and order dated 8.7.75 passed by Mr. SB Haque, Sub-Judge, Rangpur in Misc. Case No. 1 of 1975. 

 2. The relevant facts of the case in short are that, Abdul Aziz and Naziruddin Ahmed obtained a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession in Title Suit No. 96 of 1959 of the Sub-Judge's Court Rangpur and put the decree in Execution in Title Execution Case No. 34 of 1969. The judgment debtor-opposite party filed objection against the execution of the decree under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the execution case, inter alia, on the ground that the decree is not executable. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the petition holding that one of the decree holders namely, Abdul Aziz was an Indian national and his interest in the suit, property became enemy property according to the Defence of Pakistan Rules, 1965 and subsequently vested property and vested in the Govt. of Bangladesh, in view of the provisions made in The Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) (Repeal) Act 1974 (Act LV of 1974). 

 5. It appears from the petition for execution of the decree that Abdul Aziz's address is given at Patgram within district Rangpur and in the Memo of present appeal, the same address of Abdul Aziz is given. After his death, his heirs were substituted. Now even assuming that Abdul Aziz was an Indian national and as such an enemy, the learned Advocate submits that after the emergence of Bangladesh, Abdul Aziz ceased to be an enemy national, and as such, the Courts below were not justified in allowing the Misc. Case and dismissing the execution petition. In support of his contention, he referred to the Bangladesh (SC) Digest Vol-II at page 27 where it was held as follows: 

 The plaintiff-decree holder-petitioners instituted an execution case which was contested by Respondent No. 1 u/s 47 CPC. The only question was that two of the decree holders were residing in India and since 1965 they become alien residents. 

 Observed: The High Court Division had rightly noticed that section 83 of the Code is no longer operative in the present case and the execution case as a whole in its entirety may proceed at the instance of the decree holders irrespective of their residence. The point is correct. 

 7. In view of the above facts and circumstances and the legal position discussed, the appeal is allowed. The impugned orders of the courts below are hereby set aside and the case is sent back on remand to the executing court for making fresh decision, according to law and in the light of the observations made above. There will be no cost of this appeal.
